listing_view.reasoning: There is no subscription data, anchor book, grey-market signal, or basis-for-price chapter in what I was given, so there is genuinely nothing to form a listing-day view on. Indian mainboard IPOs are often priced for the seller, and with no valuation anchor I default to no view.

longterm_view.reasoning: The underlying business looks real: revenue grew from ₹3,729 million to ₹4,892 million across FY2024–FY2026, the order book roughly doubled to ₹1,586 million, free cash flow is positive and rising, and the top-10 customers are only ~24–28% of revenue, which limits concentration risk [business, page 212][business, page 216]. The score is capped because I have no ROE, ROCE, margins, or balance-sheet debt figures, so I cannot tell whether this is a high-quality business or a capital-hungry low-return one at a seller-friendly price.

governance.reasoning: No material SEBI or regulatory inspection findings are disclosed [litigation, page 366], and related-party dealings appear confined to disclosed director remuneration and shareholding [promoters, page 278]. This is only a modest positive because the prospectus is the seller's own document and I have no detail on the scale of related-party transactions.

key_risks.why_it_matters: No basis-for-price chapter or ROE/ROCE was extractable, so the ₹258–271 band cannot be tested against any return metric; overpaying is the single biggest IPO risk.
Operations including the corporate office run from third-party premises, so loss of those leases could disrupt the business that justifies the valuation.
The growth story rests partly on an order book that nearly doubled to ₹1,586 million; if margins or execution lag, the FY2026 revenue plateau (₹4,890m vs ₹4,328m) looks weaker than the headline.

answers.question: Assess this Indian IPO for listing and long-term
answers.answer: Business fundamentals are decent (growing revenue, doubling order book, positive and rising free cash flow, diversified customer base per [business, page 212][business, page 216]), but with no valuation chapter, no returns ratios, and no subscription/anchor data, I cannot say whether the ₹258–271 price is fair or how listing day will go.

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: A basis-for-price section with ROE/ROCE and peer multiples, plus the fresh issue vs offer-for-sale split — a large OFS would push my long-term score down; demonstrably high returns on capital and a primarily fresh issue would push it up.
